### 2. Your role

Structural engineer, engaged by the client and coordinated by the architect. You design and document the permanent structure. Where a specialist contractor designs an element (piles, post-tensioned slabs, specialist floors), you write its performance documentation and review the contractor's design; the contractor designs and certifies it.

### 3. Scope by stage

Price each stage that applies as a lump sum. Each stage ends at client sign-off.

| Stage | Deliverable at sign-off | Pricing |
|---|---|---|
| Concept and schematic design | Briefing; site visit; review of existing information and authority requirements; geotechnical brief and liaison; structural scheme (grid, column and wall layout and sizes, floor and roof depths, lateral stability, floor and wall system options, roof steel, transfer evaluation); input for the QS; preliminary CAD drawings for coordination | Lump sum |
| Existing structure assessment | Adequacy assessment of the existing structures the works load or connect to: extent, missing drawings, testing and opening-up needed, findings and limitations. Strengthening design is priced separately until the extent is known | Lump sum |
| Planning approval | Structural design statement for the application; responses to authority requests during assessment, up to 1 | Lump sum |
| Authority asset assessment | Specialist engineering assessment for building over or next to the water authority's assets; rail corridor interface assessment where the site adjoins rail. Program: 2 to 6 months to prepare and 3 to 6 months for the authority's review (estimate) | Lump sum |
| Design development | Coordinated design; member sizes; concrete outlines; loading plans; stairs, cantilevers and roof framing; services coordination; costing review and options; value management input | Lump sum |
| Tender documents | Drawings, specification and tender schedules; typical connection details; safety in design report; tender queries and addenda. You hold the structural design except the contractor-designed elements. | Lump sum |
| Construction documents | Construction issue; design certification for the construction certificate; 1 round(s) of peer review or certifier comments | Lump sum |
| Construction phase | 4 inspections at the hold points in your inspection schedule; RFIs; shop drawing review including contractor-designed elements; certificate of completion of the structural works based on the inspections made | Lump sum |

### 4. Allowances

Price exactly these. Work beyond an allowance needs a written instruction (section 6) and is then charged at your R3 rates.

| Item | Allowance | Item | Allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Design meetings | 4 per stage | Site visits | 1 at concept and 1 at design development |

### 5. Scope position

I = included in the fee · O = optional, price as a separate line · X = excluded (the party named does it).
Service levels in this table are set for a complex project (Class 5, Mezzanine office). Technical items follow the project's own facts.
Tell us in R6 if you disagree with any line. Do not add your own general exclusions; any you add are treated as non-compliant.

| Item | Position |
|---|---|
| Design-basis schedule: geotechnical reliance, design life, importance level, loads, wind and earthquake inputs, durability and fire-resistance coordination; missing values referred to the responsible engineer | I |
| Geotechnical brief for the client to commission | I |
| Revit model shared with the design team | I |
| Safety in design report | I |
| Value management participation | I |
| Performance specifications and a delegated-design schedule for contractor-designed elements (piles, post-tensioned slabs, specialist floors): criteria, submission, review, acceptance and certificates | I |
| Detailed design of post-tensioned slabs and piles | O |
| Shoring and piled retention design | O. Price as an option: needed only for a basement or excavation next to adjoining structures. |
| Retention, underpinning, temporary works and monitoring interfaces: designer and reviewer named, permanent and temporary loads stated | O. Price as an option: needed only where temporary support or adjoining structures are affected. |
| Temporary works and propping design | X: contractor's temporary works designer |
| Strengthening design found necessary by the existing structure assessment | O |
| Fixing design for services and equipment, including seismic restraint | O |
| Miscellaneous metalwork: balustrades, screens, sunshades, fences | O |
| Dilapidation surveys of adjoining structures | O. Price as an option: needed where excavation is next to adjoining structures. |
| Super-flat floor design | O. Price as an option: needed only if the use needs a super-flat floor. |
| Ground compaction inspections | X: geotechnical engineer (not yet engaged) |
| Demolition drawings (engineering demolition and propping design is not replaced by them) | X: the architect (to be appointed) |
| Footings affected by in-ground services | I |
| Inspection schedule by element and hold point, with notification lead time and the basis for reinspection | I |

### 6. Terms

- Engagement is under AS 4122-2010 as amended by the client's special conditions (attached). Your own terms and conditions do not apply; list any change you propose to the agreement in R6.
- Only a written instruction from the client's representative authorises a change in scope, work beyond an allowance or a change in fee, under the agreement. Work beyond an allowance without that instruction is not paid.
- Each stage ends at client sign-off, and the signed-off design is the baseline for later stages. Design development within the brief is not a variation; a change the client asks for after sign-off is assessed under the agreement.
- Correcting your own errors or omissions, and coordinating your work with information you were given, is not a variation.
- Invoice monthly against stage progress; payment within 30 days. Payment does not depend on an authority approval.
- Your proposal stays valid for 90 days.
- Send questions in writing to Project manager, pm@example.com by 2026-10-23. Answers are issued to every tenderer as numbered addenda.
- No automatic annual rate increase.
- Set-outs and bulk excavation levels are the architect's.

### 7. Evaluation

Price 40% · Relevant experience 20% · Team 20% · Methodology and program 10% · Compliance with the returnable schedules 10%. Lowest price does not automatically win.

R2 Deliverables list: For each deliverable: format, stage, review rounds, who prepares it and who receives it. Say whether editable source files are included and what reliance others may place on them. Drawing list by stage, specification, reports and certificates.
R3 Hourly rates: Rates excl. GST, used only for work authorised in writing beyond the allowances. Roles: Director · Associate · Senior engineer · Engineer · Drafting or BIM lead · Drafter. Per-meeting rates if used.
R4 Team: Named lead and their availability by stage, with % time; subconsultants and their roles. Resources must match the program in R7. Named director and project engineer; CPEng or NER.
R5 Experience: Two or three comparable projects in the last five years, each with a referee. Projects with the same class and structure type.
R6 Departures: Each departure from sections 3 to 6 and from the agreement: the clause or item, the change you propose and its effect on fee and time; or write "nil". Departures are evaluated. A general exclusion or qualification not listed here is treated as non-compliant.
R7 Program: Weeks by stage against the durations given, separating your working time, authority assessment time and the dates you need inputs from others.
R8 Insurance and compliance: Professional indemnity $10 million and public liability $20 million, with insurer and expiry; workers compensation; a quality, safety and environmental management system (certified to ISO 9001, 45001 and 14001, or an equivalent system you describe); conflicts of interest.
R9 Reimbursables: "Included in the fee" (preferred), or each item with its rate.

### Before issue — resolve or accept

**Rules await owner review**: The structural engineering services rules are a draft. Drafting and editing work; issue stays blocked until the owner marks them reviewed.

**Blocks issue — Gross floor area: sources disagree (2135 vs 2895)**: Set the one figure every firm prices from.

**Unallocated: Ground compaction inspections**: Excluded from this RFP, but the project has no geotechnical engineer package. Add one or name who does it.

**Basement or deep excavation: not established**: Priced on a printed assumption until confirmed: Shoring and piled retention design; Retention, underpinning, temporary works and monitoring interfaces: designer and reviewer named, permanent and temporary loads stated; Dilapidation surveys of adjoining structures.

**Excavation next to adjoining structures or boundaries: not established**: Priced on a printed assumption until confirmed: Shoring and piled retention design; Retention, underpinning, temporary works and monitoring interfaces: designer and reviewer named, permanent and temporary loads stated; Dilapidation surveys of adjoining structures.

**Super-flat floor needed for the use: not established**: Priced on a printed assumption until confirmed: Super-flat floor design.
